style.vernacular: No permanent civilian population since the Chagossians were removed in 1967-1973. Outside the military base on Diego Garcia, the atolls hold abandoned coconut-plantation settlements (Boddam, Takamaka, Peros Banhos) of low single-storey coral-block and render buildings with rusting corrugated roofs, a stone church and manager villa, a jetty, all swallowed by low jungle between coconut palms on white coral sand.
style.ornament: Almost none: plain gable ends, small arched or square window openings, whitewash and lime render weathered to grey-green with moss and creeper; coconut-palm timber and rusted iron roofing; a ruined stone church as the one civic landmark.

sources.what: coconut plantations from 1793, abandoned Ilois plantation houses decaying, abandoned church on Boddam (Salomon), residents removed 1967-1973, Diego Garcia naval base
Ile Boddam former main settlement: jetty, shops, offices, school, church, manager villa, hidden by thick jungle; low jungle between coconut trees; wells used by yachtsmen

chagos-airport-chagos-airport.subject: The abandoned plantation church on Ile Boddam, Salomon atoll: a small stone-and-render church with a gabled roof partly collapsed, ringed by coconut palms and jungle

sources.what: Ile Boddam had a church among its plantation buildings, now hidden by jungle; photo of abandoned church
abandoned church stands on Boddam Island in the Salomon atoll
OSM footprint 14.6 x 9.9 m, area 145 m2

chagos-airport-chagos-airport.notes: Venue is labelled "airport" in the game but there is no airstrip on Ile Boddam; the real place is an abandoned settlement island. Wikidata image for the island is the abandoned church (Eglise Boddam), so the church is modelled. Size is taken from the OSM building=ruins polygon 59 m away (14.6 x 9.9 m), which may or may not be the church itself; details (roof state, colours) are inferred from weathered coral-render ruins, not from a described photo. Render as a roofless/half-roofed ruin with overgrowth.
